title: If God Knows the Future, Do We Have Free Will?
primary_keyword: if God knows the future do we have free will
secondary_keywords: does God knowing the future remove free will
topic_cluster: Doctrine of God, providence and human responsibility
search_intent: A Christian, seeker or sceptic wants to know whether God's certain knowledge of future choices makes human freedom and moral responsibility unreal.
primary_search_query: if God knows the future do we have free will
answer_system_quote_target: God knowing the future does not mean He forces every choice. Scripture teaches that God sovereignly rules history while people make real decisions for which they are responsible. His knowledge cannot be mistaken, yet His certainty does not coerce us. The cross shows divine purpose and human guilt operating together.
likely_follow_up_questions: Does God's sovereignty make people robots?
What kind of freedom does the Bible teach?
How can God ordain an event without causing sin?
Why are people responsible if God's plan is certain?
app_conversion_path: Invite Christians to practise explaining divine sovereignty and human responsibility through Acts 2:23 without denying either truth.
cluster_role: Creates a new providence and responsibility foundation linked to the existing doctrine-of-God and philosophical-question pages.
search_trend_evidence: Fresh checks on 3 August 2026 returned several exact and near-exact pages, a current philosophical discussion and a recent dedicated explainer. Results confirm durable evergreen demand, while many answers either reduce the issue to foreknowledge alone or do not clearly hold sovereignty and responsibility together.
duplicate_check_summary: Passed against blog/content-plan.json, blog/index.html, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, all visible article URLs and recent commits. Existing pages address God's existence, hiddenness, Trinity, salvation and Christology, but none claims the query family of divine foreknowledge, providence, human choice and responsibility.

full_bank_accounting_counts.method: Compared the full approved question bank with published source IDs and repository-wide topic coverage, excluded used IDs and close search-intent duplicates, ranked the remaining evergreen candidates, and deeply evaluated the strongest Monday options. Card add003 is ordinary public-safe Q&A content and contains no premium branching material.

theological_framework: Presbyterian and Reformed, using Scripture and the Westminster Confession of Faith on providence and creaturely willing as the primary doctrinal frame.
readability_check: Short sentences, plain words, active voice and compact paragraphs support the grade 9 or lower target.
editorial_note: No standalone FAQ section or FAQPage schema. Uses the current canonical static article template.
